accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE National Curriculum in England, Year 1 Animals including humans ('describe and compare the structure of a variety of common animals') and Year 2 Living things and their habitats (minibeasts in micro-habitats), and NGSS 1-LS1-1 (animals use external parts to survive). Facts checked against the Natural History Museum and RSPB/Royal Entomological Society minibeast guides: insects (ants, beetles, bees, grasshoppers, ladybirds) have six legs; spiders have eight and are arachnids, not insects; earthworms have no legs and move by rings of muscle with bristles (setae) gripping the soil, and burrow; slugs and snails glide on one muscular foot over mucus at roughly a millimetre per second; grasshoppers jump with enlarged hind legs; butterflies and bees fly with wings. The race outcome (grasshopper, then ant, then snail) matches these speeds. Parameterised items 8−n, 6−k, a stay positive at every corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the errors reported in primary science research on children's ideas about animals (Nuffield Primary SPACE 'Variety of life'; Bell & Barker 1982 on the narrow meaning of 'animal'; ASE Primary Science minibeast guidance): all minibeasts are insects and a spider is an insect (step 3 count, challenge tags all and legs, mastery m3), worms have tiny legs or walk (step 1 worm feedback, predict option 'walks on tiny legs', tags walk), slugs crawl on legs (slug feedback), feelers or the head do the moving (step 2 wrong-part feedback, tags feel and eyes), more legs or being 'a minibeast' means fast (race: the snail loses to the six-legged ant, tags snail and tie), and anything with wings flies the same way (build step: wings override legs, with feedback).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagmbmove is built on one mechanism: a minibeast's body parts decide how it moves. The learner picks a movement and the creature then animates that way (crawl, fly with flapping wings, slither with a travelling body wave, jump in arcs), taps the specific moving part on a large drawn body, counts legs leg by leg, races three movers and assembles a creature from wings, legs and long back legs whose movement is computed from the parts. It differs from flagbug (backbone check, bug hunt under logs, hand-lens leg count then sort), flagmbhab (damp/dark choice chambers and micro-habitats) and flagcoat (vertebrate coverings). The gate reports under 30% shingle overlap with every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each idea is met in the lab before the text states it: choosing 'crawl' for the worm is rejected because it has no legs, then its body wave is seen; tapping the feelers on a grasshopper is rejected and the long back legs are confirmed; counting eight spider legs triggers 'a spider is not an insect'; the race shows slime-gliding is slow; and building a mover shows wings make it fly even when legs are added, back legs make it jump, and removing every leg makes it slither.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option that the lab disproves: 'It walks on tiny legs' / 'It cannot move' for the worm (the worm slithers without legs), 'its feelers' / 'its head' for the grasshopper jump (rejected on tap), '6' or '10' legs for a spider (the count stops at 8), and 'the snail' or 'the ant' to win (the grasshopper reaches the leaf first and the snail barely moves). Each task completion echoes the locked-in choice.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions, two wrong options each, every one with its own message: walk (walking needs legs; worms squeeze and stretch), fly (flying needs wings), feel (feelers touch and smell), eyes (eyes see; back legs jump), eight (8 legs is a spider), four (count 3 a side), all (not all minibeasts are insects), legs (legs are not enough; exactly 6), slug (no wings, slithers on slime), wormfly (no wings, slithers and digs), snail (slow slime vs fast ant) and tie (6 running legs beat sliding). In-lab feedback also names the slip, e.g. 'That is its feelers. Feelers touch and smell. It does not make it jump.'

readability.evidence: validate_lessons.py passes the learner limits; the kid paragraphs score about grade 1 and the adult text about grade 6. Canvas text uses one short line per goal ('How does the ant move?', 'Count the ant's legs. Tap each leg.'), and the movement words are the four concrete verbs crawl, fly, slither and jump throughout. Feedback lines are one or two short sentences.

no_filler.evidence: No filler pattern matches. Each step has one job (movement words, body clues, leg counts, speed, cause and effect in a build), and every feedback line carries a body part, a number or a reason. Item explanations give the reason (no legs, 6 a side, slime) rather than repeating the prompt.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px width in light and dark, before and after Show me for every step. After the first pass the minibeasts were enlarged (scale up from 9% to 14% of the width) so legs and feelers are tappable, the race start moved right so the 1st/2nd/3rd labels no longer cover the snail, and the build pads now wrap 'Long back legs' onto two lines instead of clipping. The four movement pads and three part pads are full-width rows about 50 px tall, and every move is repeated by large buttons below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Everything is doable with buttons: crawl/fly/slither/jump ('It can crawl'), named body parts ('Tap the long back legs'), 'Count the next leg' and 'It has no legs', 'Start the race' and 'Grasshopper next', and 'Add wings' / 'Remove legs' / 'Test my minibeast'. After each move the canvas aria-label states the scene, e.g. 'A worm. Does it crawl, fly, slither or jump?' or 'Goal: jump. Parts on: Long back legs.'. Challenge feedback is an aria-live status. walk.cjs reports axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors; the canvas keeps a light card in dark mode.
